definitions.explanation: The real nature or identity of something. Almost exclusively used in the negative expression 得体の知れない (of unknown nature, mysterious, suspicious).

examples.japanese: {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{生物|せいぶつ}を{見|み}つけた。
{得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{不安|ふあん}に{襲|おそ}われた。
examples.english: I was overcome by a mysterious anxiety.

examples.japanese: {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{男|おとこ}が{家|いえ}の{前|まえ}をうろうろしていたので、{警察|けいさつ}に{連絡|れんらく}した。
examples.english: A suspicious man was loitering in front of the house, so I called the police.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used in the set phrase {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない, meaning "of unknown nature," "mysterious," or "unidentifiable." This expression modifies nouns to convey suspicion, eeriness, or the unsettling quality of something whose true identity cannot be determined. The standalone word {得体|えたい} is rarely used outside this pattern.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{人|ひと}: a suspicious/mysterious person
- {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{不安|ふあん}: a vague, inexplicable anxiety
- {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{物|もの}: an unidentifiable thing
- {得体|えたい}の{知|し}れない{液体|えきたい}: an unknown liquid
